In [[commutative algebra]], the '''Fitting ideals''' of a [[finitely generated module]] over a [[commutative ring]] describe the obstructions to generating the module by a given number of elements. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|author-link=Hans Fitting|first=Hans |last=Fitting|year=1936}}.

==Definition==
If ''M'' is a finitely generated module over a commutative ring ''R'' generated by elements ''m''<sub>1</sub>,...,''m''<sub>''n''</sub>
with relations

:<math>a_{j1}m_1+\cdots + a_{jn}m_n=0\ (\text{for }j = 1, 2, \dots) </math>

then the ''i''th Fitting ideal <math>\operatorname{Fitt}_i(M)</math> of ''M'' is generated by the minors (determinants of submatrices) of order <math>n-i</math> of the matrix <math>a_{jk}</math>. 
The Fitting ideals do not depend on the choice of generators and relations  of ''M''.

Some authors defined the Fitting ideal <math>I(M)</math> to be the first nonzero Fitting ideal <math>\operatorname{Fitt}_i(M)</math>.

==Properties==
The Fitting ideals are increasing

: <math>\operatorname{Fitt}_0(M) \subseteq \operatorname{Fitt}_1(M) \subseteq \operatorname{Fitt}_2(M) \subseteq \cdots </math>

If ''M'' can be generated by ''n'' elements then Fitt<sub>''n''</sub>(''M'') =&nbsp;''R'', and if ''R'' is local the converse holds.  We have Fitt<sub>0</sub>(''M'')&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;Ann(''M'') (the annihilator of&nbsp;''M''), and Ann(''M'')Fitt<sub>''i''</sub>(''M'')&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;Fitt<sub>''i''&minus;1</sub>(''M''), so in particular if ''M'' can be generated by ''n'' elements then Ann(''M'')<sup>''n''</sup>&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;Fitt<sub>0</sub>(''M'').

==Examples==
If ''M'' is free of rank ''n'' then the Fitting ideals <math>\operatorname{Fitt}_i(M)</math> are zero for ''i''<''n'' and ''R'' for&nbsp;''i''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;''n''. 

If ''M'' is a finite [[abelian group]] of order <math>|M|</math> (considered as a module over the integers) then the Fitting ideal <math>\operatorname{Fitt}_0(M)</math> is the ideal <math>(|M|)</math>.

The [[Alexander polynomial]] of a knot is a generator of the Fitting ideal of the first homology of the infinite abelian cover of the [[knot complement]].

== Fitting image ==
The zeroth Fitting ideal can be used also to give a variant of the notion of [[scheme-theoretic image]] of a morphism, a variant that behaves well in families.   Specifically, given a [[finite morphism]] of [[noetherian scheme]]s <math>f \colon X \rightarrow Y</math>, the <math>\mathcal{O}_Y</math>-module <math>f_* \mathcal{O}_X</math> is [[coherent sheaf|coherent]], so we may define <math>\operatorname{Fitt}_0(f_* \mathcal{O}_X)</math> as a coherent sheaf of <math>\mathcal{O}_Y</math>-ideals; the corresponding [[closed subscheme]] of <math>Y</math> is called the '''Fitting image''' of ''f''.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Eisenbud|first1=David|author1-link=David Eisenbud|last2=Harris| first2=Joe |author2-link=Joe Harris (mathematician)|title=The Geometry of Schemes |publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]] |isbn=0-387-98637-5 |pages=219 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/b97680}}</ref>{{fact|date=August 2023}}
